nodes.label: Free Host-Minute Quota
nodes.community_name: Room Flow and P2P Flawless Execution Plan
nodes.evidence_excerpt: - **PD2 — free plan quota (owner decision 2026-06-12):** the free (`watcher`) plan gets **30 host-minutes per day** instead of an active-room-count limit. Zoom-style semantics: the quota burns only while the user's *own* room has **2 or more connected participants** (solo testing is free); joining someone else's room never burns the guest's quota, whatever their plan — paid hosts can always invite free friends. Quota resets per UTC day. At 5 remaining minutes the room receives a warning event; at 0 the room ends gracefully with an upgrade prompt. Paid plans (`nakama`, `junkie`) stay unmetered. The 4-hour `last_active_at` staleness rule remains for room lifecycle hygiene (zombie cleanup, dashboards), but is no longer the plan-limit mechanism.

nodes.label: Catalog Snapshot And Variants
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Bounded snapshots and server-derived aliases establish exact identity and regional totals without loading the full catalog during normal reads.

nodes.label: Existing Worker Live-Room Authority Remains Unchanged
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: existing worker live-room authority remains unchanged
nodes.rationale: Shared-session identity stays room_id plus room_generation plus source_generation. Worker authority validates actual source fingerprint, not logical keys. Personal deletion preserves other participants.

nodes.label: Schema 3 Cutover
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: The coordinated staging cutover is complete; main/production promotion and authenticated acceptance remain separate.

nodes.label: Canonical Deletion Safety
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Fence canonical identity; delayed resolution preserves original time/owner/generation. Never reuse catalog revisions after delete/recreate. Full clear advances requester generation; episode deletion keeps catalog.

nodes.label: Canonical Crunchyroll Identity
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Keys derive exactly from provider series ID, season identifier, and episode identifier. Locale, labels, numbering, audio and mutable slugs are not identity. Distinct provider seasons remain distinct; unresolved identity stays in the bounded outbox.

nodes.label: Canonical Progress
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: One progress row per account/logical episode prevents audio double-counting. Completion is sticky; resume uses the latest actually watched variant and its own position/duration. Adapt existing indexed summaries directly.

nodes.label: Catalog Completeness Gate
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Exact totals require stable identity/region, complete traversal, raw-total agreement before collapse/filtering, unique aliases, deterministic order, known availability, immutable context, and count/byte bounds. Failure or ambiguity produces partial.

nodes.label: Clean Start Decision
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: The user states there are no real users and old test history has no product value. Preservation, import, backfill and reconciliation are no longer requirements. This amendment is not implementation or remote-transition approval.

nodes.label: Provider Localized Catalog Labels
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Capture display locale immutably and persist provider-returned labels without translation. Accepted labels override observed labels. Failed same-region locale refresh retains the previous exact localized bundle; audio/subtitles are separate.

nodes.label: Regional Availability Denominator
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Counts released logical episodes listed as available in provider-reported region, not entitlement. Unknown availability prevents completeness. Historical completion remains; exact completion intersects the current available set.

nodes.label: Revisioned Catalog Begin And Commit
nodes.community_name: Watch History Crunchyroll Catalog Progress Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Authenticated begin allocates monotonic revisions; commit checks schema/generation/context/fences/bounds/hash and replaces atomically. Latest revision wins. Region changes suppress exact data; same-region refresh retains the accepted bundle. Collection alone creates no watched cards.

nodes.label: Scoped Test History Transition

## Task 2: Establish actual backup and restore capability

**Files:** Read `scripts/production-history-rehearsal.mjs`, the existing rehearsal receipt and preservation runbook. Add aggregate recovery identifiers/results to the release audit; never add a dump or user row to Git/CI artifacts.

**Interfaces:** Consumes the exact project identity and stable 35-version baseline; produces an identified recovery artifact/checkpoint, proven restore procedure, measured recovery duration and finite retention/owner record.
nodes.norm_label: historical: acl correction and conditional role recovery verified on second target
nodes.rationale: Historical evidence only: the September 13 owner correction superseded the preservation campaign and prefixes 38/50 as release gates. Completed receipts remain retained; the ordinary production migration subsequently completed. Local offline and PostgreSQL 17 ACL/rollback proof, policy review and capture-source review remain separate evidence. Fresh guarded captures passed every condition and independent review explicitly accepted the corrected second application recovery. Later targets require their own evidence; first-run failure and production gates remain unchanged.

## Exit and failure decisions

Before any migration commits, abort to the unchanged old DB/runtime while retaining the stable backup. After a committed migration/reset, retain maintenance and choose reviewed forward completion or a full baseline DB + matching runtime restore. Never restore schema1 rows into v3 live tables or use only an old Web redeploy as rollback.

Main promotion and runtime release are not equivalent: the candidate deliberately holds automatic production deployment. A merged PR is not a successful DB transition, and a green DB receipt is not a reopened service. Record every step's actual evidence and stop at the first unmet prerequisite.

nodes.label: Bounded-Shape Watch History Outbox

nodes.label: Cursor-Bounded Title Projection
nodes.rationale: The additive projection selects a title page before transporting progress and limits requester-owned session enrichment, eliminating account-wide aggregation and session fanout.

nodes.label: Durable History Deletion Fences
nodes.rationale: Episode and title fences reject queued pre-delete events and remain durable; full clear advances the account generation before old-generation fences can be removed.

nodes.label: Idempotency-First Conflict Ordering
nodes.rationale: Receipts are checked before mutation, while normalized observation time plus server order resolves new events without allowing retries or future-skewed clocks to poison canonical progress.

nodes.label: Migration-First Production Deployment Ordering

Group and episode identities are stable canonical IDs, not labels or season numbers; group/title progress is stored once rather than copied to accounts. Membership boundaries and versions protect pending checkpoints without creating watched-interval or meeting logs. Group-binding uniqueness is by roomId across all generations: a new roomGeneration never allows another binding or reopens terminal recording.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Persistent Group History
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target persistent group history
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. A persistent group owns one independent shared result per canonical provider/title across temporary rooms. All current members see the same result, including members added after past viewing. Mine holds personal viewing, including guests and ordinary rooms, manual marks and explicit imports; active group viewing is not copied automatically. No host transfer, ordinary-member launch, group chat, meeting history or new invitation system enters the MVP.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Reached And Resume Positions
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target reached and resume positions
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. EpisodeProgress separates monotonic maxReachedPosition, latest ordered resumePosition and sticky completed within one owner, canonical episode and compatible video timeline since reset. Confirmed playback starts automatic progress; opening, hover or paused preparation does not. A viewer joining E5 at 12 minutes and reaching 18 stores 18 minutes for E5 without proving 0-12 coverage or completing E1-E4. Rewind can move resume backward but cannot reduce reached maximum or completion without explicit reset/replacement.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Terminal Group Session
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target terminal group session
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Group recording has no-group, waiting, active and closed states separate from room lifecycle. One other current group member entering the player activates the session; actual host playback advances progress. Waiting host playback is personal. The last other member's confirmed departure fixes the shared point and permanently closes group recording for that room, even if unrelated guests remain. Returning, source changes or Worker restarts cannot reopen it; a new room continues the same group. Host departure ends the room without transfer.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Versioned Together API
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target versioned together api
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. A dedicated versioned Together DTO and /api/watch-history/v3/together namespace provide group reads and shared-progress management. Existing solo/shared session type is distinct from personal/group history destination and cannot merely be renamed. Contracts cover read, bind, launch/recover, capture/reconcile, edit/reset, preview/apply import and leave/archive, while extending existing join/invite/quota/callback routes. Protocol schemas precede all consumers and expose meaningful access, terminal, conflict, upgrade, quota, source and authority errors.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: Together MVP Revision 2
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. TARGET only, dated 2026-09-07: consolidated specification before implementation, migrations or release. It replaces the previous file revision and working model review. Automatic companies, composition/date-based history, mandatory copying of group viewing to Mine and watched-interval coverage are superseded and excluded. Documentation is not deployment permission or acceptance evidence.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Bounded Checkpoint Queue
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target bounded checkpoint queue
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Latest-plus-terminal compaction also retains the maximum unacknowledged reached position so a rewind cannot erase unsent progress. Queue keys include account, destination, group session, source generation and episode; acknowledgements remove only the confirmed version. Existing heartbeat/event publication remains, pages are at most 50 and packets at most 64 KiB. The 86400-second room-history offline grace permits delivery of valid earlier data, not a day-long active room or reopening a closed session; failures remain visible.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Checkpoint Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Versioned checkpoints carry account/session scope, event ID, canonical source, current and maximum positions, duration/ended, local sequence and verified room/group-session context. Only the host may propose shared progress. A room-history attestation alone cannot prove an active group session: Worker-confirmed generation/order and durable final boundaries are checked by Web. Reliable lifecycle delivery covers binding, membership, source and departure. One transaction validates identity, reset and session fences before updating exactly one destination and revision.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Compatibility Migration
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Preserve existing personal v3 data, including old shared viewing; do not infer new groups or shared results from old sessions, people, dates or invites. Initialize legacy maxReachedPosition from stored position while preserving resume/completed and inventing no past maximum. Existing private recipient lists require explicit owner confirmation of a shared name before disclosure. Old clients cannot enter or write group recording until upgraded, including old reconcile/SQL/queued paths. Additive DB, matched Web/protocol, Worker and extension/site precede capability activation; rollback closes group writes while retaining data and compatible reads.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Completion And Catalog Totals
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target completion and catalog totals
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Valid ended or reached position at least 90 percent of reliable duration sets completed for both personal and group progress. Unknown duration does not justify a percentage. Ninety-percent completion still resumes the saved position until ended; only ended proposes the next known released main episode, with no invented gaps or automatic Specials. Season/title counts use completed main episodes over a confirmed available catalog, with Specials separate. Reached seconds are progress markers, not actual watch-time or billable host-minutes.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Consent And Access
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target consent and access
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Existing supported-source and YouTube-history consent survives. The creator's permission controls automatic group recording, while each guest controls their personal capture; invites, binding, import and reads do not silently enable capture. Unavailable group capture is visibly suspended without fallback to Mine. Current members see shared results but no private personal history or secrets; guests receive no group name/history. Revocation blocks new server actions and invalidates connected caches without claiming instantaneous offline erasure.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Entitlements And Archive
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target entitlements and archive
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Existing owner-group limits remain Free 1, Plus 5, Pro 15; joining another group consumes none, room capacity follows host plan and billing host-minutes are unchanged. Member plan does not truncate a shared result. Legacy watch-library title/day constants do not authorize new v3 retention cleanup. Archive closes group recording and future launches but preserves current-member read/import access. Group clear affects only its scope; creator account deletion grants no ownership transfer and preserves others' independent personal copies.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Filter And Cache Semantics
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target filter and cache semantics
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Search/resource/date filters apply to accessible group history before pagination without recomputing shared progress. A participant filter means current group member, not proven historical attendee. No groups, no history, no matches, lost access, unavailable source and load failure are distinct states. Account/group/access-version caches never grant fresh rights or launch offline; loading cannot replace confirmed progress with false zero. Controls remain keyboard accessible and respect reduced motion.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Membership And Creator Rights
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target membership and creator rights
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. The immutable creator adds accepted friends without a separate membership acceptance and alone controls group launches, membership, archive and shared edits. Current members can read shared name/composition/progress and import it; guests cannot. Membership is independent of invite method and room admission. Removal, leaving or friendship termination revokes access without erasing group results or personal imports, and a remaining room occupant becomes a tracking guest.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET One Time Group Import
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target one time group import
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. An accessible group's selected title can be previewed and atomically copied into Mine. Default merge preserves personal completions and resume while adding missing completed episodes and farther compatible partial progress; exact Replace this title and use-group-resume are separate explicit choices. Exact episodes are copied without filling gaps, dates, attendance or ongoing linkage. Source and target versions and access are rechecked at apply; stable operation IDs make lost-response retries safe.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET One Time Room Binding
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target one time room binding
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. The existing player flow creates a room before inviting a group. Its first explicit Invite & track group or equivalent selection binds one group once after server checks; personal viewing before binding is not reclassified. Later invites only add recipients and cannot switch history to another group. Send-time snapshots, existing Inbox/Copy invite delivery and semantic dedupe are reused. A delivery failure does not undo a confirmed binding or create another room.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Ordering And Reset Fences
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target ordering and reset fences
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Server session ordinal, source generation and host sequence order group resume. A valid late old-room checkpoint may extend its episode's reached maximum but cannot move a newer room's resume. Original event boundaries, not arrival time, determine personal/group destination. Event dedupe, optimistic result revision and reset cutoff are independent fences. Resetting E2 must not revive from stale writes or discard pending E3; stale takeover tabs, accounts, generations and incompatible video writers are rejected.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Personal Group Routing
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target personal group routing
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. During an active group session, the validated creator-host supplies the group's position and current group members do not receive an automatic personal copy. Guests always record only their own player; ordinary rooms, waiting viewers and post-close viewing use Mine. Group recording requires binding, host role, another current member actually in the player, allowed source capture and current authority. Routing belongs to the specific player/tab: independent video in another tab cannot borrow group authority. Two devices of one account are not two viewers.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Reconnect Grace And Order
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target reconnect grace and order
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Explicit departure closes without waiting, while reload/BFCache/transport loss uses ROOM_DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS=60000. Host checkpoints remain pending while the last other member's presence is unresolved, avoiding Mine/Together flicker. Recovery or another valid member arriving before final departure confirmation preserves the open session; after closure no arrival reopens it. Server ordering resolves join/removal/departure, and hibernation, participant buffering, ads and media toggles are not departures.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Staging Acceptance
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. T01-T64 are future acceptance requirements, not tests already passed. Implement protocol invariants, durable storage/access, reliable Worker/Web lifecycle, extension writers/queues, Together launch/invites and website editor/import before coordinated staging delivery. Required proof spans SQL/RPC, affected plane checks/tests, runtime/room harness, smoke and a real loaded artifact with creator, member and outside guest across departure, grace, resume, import and reset. Main/production need separate authorization; cards-only or SQL-only work is incomplete.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Together Presentation
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. One canonical provider/title card contains a group selector, season/Specials selector, bounded episode grid and stable selected-episode detail. Dates, meeting cards, personal lag warnings and attendance claims are excluded. Selection is persisted by account/title and group/season; group switching never launches or invites. The grid independently shows reached progress, completion and selection, and its action uses displayed resume rather than hidden maximum. Films remain one detail without invented seasons.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Verified Group Launch
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target verified group launch
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. Only the creator launches or resumes after server access, revision, source, quota and active-room checks. A suitable active room is reused without surprise seek; otherwise one idempotent operation opens the verified source at the displayed point on pause and then the existing invite drawer, without automatic recipient resend. Another active room is not silently ended. Members receive Join only for an allowed running room. Source identity/generation and video compatibility prevent guessed seconds or cross-provider misuse. If the group's active room already has a different title/episode, show its actual source and return action; the old card cannot create another room or change playback implicitly.

nodes.label: Deferred Together: TARGET Website History Editor
nodes.norm_label: deferred together: target website history editor
nodes.rationale: Deferred historical design as of 2026-09-08; not the current MVP. One website editor serves Mine and creator-owned groups, with the result owner and destructive scope explicit. Canonical supported titles allow episode/season/Specials/movie marks, partial reached position, separate resume and scoped clear without invented sessions, dates or watch minutes. Season marking affects only the shown known set. Mark unwatched resets that episode's progress; editing an actively recorded result or pending launch requires stopping that viewing, enforced server-side without seeking other players.

SQL cron success is not HTTP drain success or user receipt; lost transient work leaves the durable outbox intact.

nodes.label: Server Confirmed Quota Renewal
nodes.description: At zero the server is checked; offline shows Retry. Confirmed exhaustion survives delayed final usage persistence in the same UTC day. A new day or confirmed paid access shows renewal.
nodes.rationale: The user explicitly creates a room through normal admission; a countdown never grants minutes or starts a room.

nodes.label: Additive Quota Delivery And Rollback
nodes.description: Delivery uses staging API and compatible ZIP, CI and artifact checks, then a promotion PR and private production ZIP. No migration, new secrets or public ZIP are needed; rollback restores prior Web and ZIP.
nodes.rationale: The GET is additive and unused by old clients; installed-ZIP acceptance remains separate from automated and isolated browser evidence.

nodes.label: Authenticated Room Quota View
nodes.description: GET /api/me/room-quota verifies bearer or cookie session and owner header, freshly resolves the plan, and returns serverTime with remainingSeconds and resetAt or quota:null for paid access. Responses are private,no-store; staging bypass is limited to this bearer GET.
nodes.rationale: Client data cannot select the authoritative day or remaining allowance.

nodes.label: Bounded Owner Fenced Quota Recheck
nodes.description: Parallel requests coalesce, attempts have a five-second minimum interval and ten-second timeout, and a token refresh runs once with owner checks before and after. Responses for another account are rejected.
nodes.rationale: Account changes must not allow a stale response to assign another account quota.

nodes.label: Host And Guest Quota End Notice
nodes.description: September15 UI consumes ROOM_ENDED.reason: host gets server-UTC-anchored reset countdown, guests get host-limit explanation. Monotonic elapsed time and sleep/clock rechecks require server confirmation at zero. Worker/admission stay authoritative; installed-ZIP proof is separate.
nodes.norm_label: host and guest quota end notice
nodes.rationale: A display countdown must not grant quota or mistake local clock changes for permission to host.
nodes.evidence_excerpt:
## Follow-up: Free quota reset notice, 2026-09-15

The overlay now consumes `ROOM_ENDED.reason` to distinguish host quota exhaustion
from ordinary closure. Only the host gets the reset countdown; guests get a
host-limit explanation. A new authenticated read-only quota view anchors the
countdown to server UTC and monotonic elapsed time, rechecks after sleep/clock
changes, and requires server confirmation at zero. The existing Worker and room
admission remain authoritative. No media, SQL or live protocol changes are needed.
See the [quota follow-up](2026-09-08-personal-history-and-plans-mvp.md#free-quota-countdown-follow-up-2026-09-15)
for request/account fences, offline behavior and rollback. Private installed-ZIP
acceptance remains separate from automated lifecycle and isolated browser tests.

nodes.label: Server UTC Monotonic Countdown
nodes.description: The countdown pairs server request-reception time with performance.now() at client request start, accounting for request latency. A response spanning sleep or a clock jump is discarded completely. Date.now() only detects discontinuities requiring a fresh server request.
nodes.rationale: Opening, visibility return, connectivity restoration and zero refresh the status without per-second server polling.

nodes.label: Free Quota Countdown Card

# Репетиция перехода на staging — 29 сентября 2026

Владелец явно разрешил включение новой модели для ручной репетиции и подготовил
комнаты на Free и платном аккаунтах. Это отдельная операция после поставки
оптимизации Durable Objects. Полная ручная матрица не объявляется принятой.

## Переключение и проверенное окружение

- Staging Supabase: `cyppqpprkygjloyfvvvj`.
- Web: `dpl_4pPLCVC4CiK6x6TXhBvEQvTD62ww`, READY, staging alias,
  source `73ea22d5f021b4650ad2cb83acd24a91435f4b76`.
- Worker: `f7942d07-cb7a-473e-9484-c26768ea04c2`, 100% staging traffic.
- Операция: `e58cd271-ce00-4916-a074-e3a184175d48`, ожидаемая revision 1
  записана до SQL. Активация штатной `activate_paid_hosting_v1`, без ручного
  изменения комнат или сброса trial.
- **T: 2026-09-29 15:48:48.800820 UTC**, revision 2, trials enabled.
- Scheduler enabled, environment строго staging. Personal history policy active.
- Секреты не выгружались и не ротировались. Перед T настоящий pg_net запрос
  получил HTTP 200 и точное `{"ok":true}` от staging drain.

## Комнаты и аккаунты

При первом чтении были две открытые Free-комнаты и одна Plus-комната.
Одна Free-комната завершилась в 15:46:00.415 UTC, до T; причина этого завершения
в рамках репетиции не устанавливалась, и оно не засчитывается как эффект cutover.
На момент T оставалась одна открытая Free-комната: target_count = 1.

- Выбранная Free-комната: durable fence/ended в 15:48:50.273 UTC,
  **1.472180 секунды после T**; finalized в 15:48:52.503 UTC,
  **3.702180 секунды после T**.
- Outbox: одна попытка, одна завершенная цель, нет pending targets/leases.
  Активных назначений в закрытой комнате нет.
- Plus-комната осталась live, ended_at NULL, два активных назначения в момент
  readback. Это серверное состояние, не самостоятельное доказательство
  непрерывности видео/аудио в браузерах.
- Распределение аккаунтов до и после: 61 Free, 1 Plus. Полный отсортированный
  fingerprint строк subscriptions совпал; подписки не изменились.
- Trial rows после переключения: 0. Включение предложения не запускает пробный
  период автоматически и не списывает деньги с Free-аккаунтов.

Vercel в окне 15:48:40–15:50:00 UTC: drain HTTP 200,
`claimed: 1, completed: 1, pending: 0, errors: 0`; error/fatal logs отсутствуют.
Scheduler прочитал успешный ACK в 15:49:00 UTC. Это первая успешная реальная
цепочка pg_net → Web → Worker → Web/PostgREST для одной открытой комнаты;
один замер не устанавливает гарантированную задержку при нагрузке/отказах.

## Старые платежные сессии

До T проверены две pre-T reservation в AniDachi sandbox, livemode false.
Одна старая неоплаченная сессия была еще open: она завершена штатным Stripe
`checkout sessions expire`, повторное API-чтение подтвердило expired/unpaid,
subscription NULL. Другая была complete/paid и уже соответствовала активной
Plus-подписке. Обе reservation приведены к подтвержденным состояниям штатной
`complete_subscription_checkout_reservation_v1`; подписка сохранена.
Stripe MCP не предоставил операцию expire в результатах поиска, поэтому для
этого использована Stripe Shell внутри явно выбранного AniDachi sandbox.
Локальный операционный receipt хранит точные ссылки и исходный fingerprint;
контактные данные и платежные ссылки в этот документ не включены.

## Ручная приемка продолжается

- [x] Разрешение владельца и проверка окружения перед T.
- [x] Активация staging, выбор только оставшейся Free-комнаты, durable closure
  и сверка всех целей с отсутствием активных назначений.
- [x] Серверное сохранение Plus-комнаты, аккаунтов и подписок.
- [x] Владелец подтвердил: «да плюс осталась а фри закрылись». Это ручное
  подтверждение сохранения Plus и закрытия Free на старом расширении; отдельная
  проверка очистки каждого аудио/видеотрека этим ответом не установлена.
- [x] Отказ повторного Free-create и разрешенный Free-join к Plus на старом ZIP.
  Владелец подтвердил оба действия: «да, все работает как нужно». Точный текст
  отказа и отдельный вход к Pro этим ответом не проверены.
- [x] Владелец оформил trial Plus через сайт и сообщил об успешном результате.
  Read-only проверка 29 сентября 16:30 UTC: Stripe Sandbox и Supabase согласованы,
  status trialing, account plan/effective grant Plus, ровно 72 часа — с
  29 сентября 16:00:51 UTC до 2 октября 16:00:51 UTC. Способ оплаты сохранен;
  charge_automatically, cancel_at_period_end false, затем $7.99 USD/месяц.
  Это подтверждает начало trial и серверные права, не будущую успешную оплату.
- [x] Создание комнаты после trial на старом ZIP и вход бесплатного участника.
  Владелец подтвердил оба действия: «проверил, все работает».
- [ ] Отдельный checkout trial Pro и остальные платежные переходы.
- [x] Базовый сценарий нового staging ZIP `59d6e80e`: окно выбора плана у Free,
  правильное отображение trial Plus и создание комнаты, вход Free-гостя
  и синхронизация. Владелец подтвердил: «да, все работает как положено».
  Перед этим SHA-256 предоставленного ZIP совпал с зафиксированным артефактом.
- [ ] Полная lifecycle/P11/история/ошибки оплаты и recovery-матрица; в частности
  отмена, окончание trial и последующее списание отдельно еще не приняты.

Дизайн сайта и годовой план обсуждаются следующим отдельным блоком на staging;
в эту операцию не входили. Новый код, ZIP, main/production и Store не выпускались.
Не сбрасывать T и не воскрешать закрытые Free-комнаты ради повторения: следовать
[runbook восстановления](cutover-operations.md). Следующие испытания идут при
уже включенной модели; повторная активация с новым UUID запрещена.

SEO evidence hierarchy and URL stability
nodes.description: Google docs precede site analytics, reproducible tests, third-party studies and speculative patents. During freeze enrich existing winners; no route creation/rename/delete, canonical retarget, redirects, noindex, crawl shrinkage or pillar-intent rewrite without owner approval and GSC evidence.
nodes.rationale: Preserve ranking equity and prevent thin or cannibalizing URL growth.

nodes.label: SEO publication and keyword validation
nodes.description: Require freeze exception, full inventory/GSC intent ownership, distinct content, parent hub plus two inbound links, honest dates/review, product/legal truth and first-touch attribution. Reject below10 monthly searches absent unique commercial value.
nodes.rationale: New pages must justify their intent and discovery path before publication.

nodes.label: YouTube sibling cluster
nodes.description: YouTube pillar owns watch-party head intent; distinct how-to, free, Discord, alternatives and long-distance URLs own their intents. Keyword numbers are snapshots; re-pull before proposals, use platform-specific pricing, narrow tags and correct desktop-watch limits.

nodes.label: Crunchyroll conversion and intent ownership
nodes.description: Crunchyroll pillar and owned how-to/free/Discord/alternatives intents remain independent of anime vertical. Each viewer supplies own Crunchyroll access; platform-specific copy, narrow related tags and HowTo parity prevent drift.

nodes.label: Platform and anime vertical hierarchy
nodes.description: Anime is a vertical containing genre/title content; Crunchyroll and YouTube are flat sibling platform pillars. Do not rename ranked routes or parent YouTube under anime; unsupported future platforms are not promised.

nodes.label: Editorial trust and title-specific value
nodes.description: Verified social proof, primary competitor sources and verification dates, honest schema/pricing, observable pacing or episode properties and specific FAQ answers are required.
nodes.rationale: Avoid fabricated authority and boilerplate group-watch praise.

nodes.label: Residual SEO agent ambiguities
nodes.description: Alternatives subsection asks for a mid CTA while the current global card cap allows only above-fold plus end. A text-link interpretation is plausible but not explicit; source ambiguity is flagged rather than permission for a third card.

nodes.label: Session first-touch marketing attribution
nodes.description: seo_landing_path, seo_referrer and seo_utm capture the first marketing landing, including client navigation from an auth route; Checkout Session and Subscription preserve equivalent metadata.

nodes.label: Download deduplication and installation evidence
nodes.description: Client download click and server GET share insert_id for Amplitude deduplication; server HTTP also records the event. Downloads/clicks do not prove install and extension_detected is retired.
nodes.rationale: Analytics must not convert a download or click into installation evidence.

nodes.label: Field web-vital reporting
nodes.description: pagehide/visibilitychange reports LCP, INP, CLS with value/rating/path/template; CLS is multiplied by1000. Reporting does not alter rendering or core flows.

nodes.label: Full-route portfolio measurement
nodes.description: seo:portfolio inventories all public sitemap URLs, joins GSC queries/pages and GA4 sessions/channels/key events, and suggests actions. Coverage still needs Search Console; growth waits for30/60/90-day cohort review.

nodes.label: Current subscription and history product copy
nodes.description: Live features are synchronized players, on-player chat/reactions, voice/video and personal history on supported desktop Crunchyroll/YouTube. Free joins paid/trial hosts; hosting needs own Plus/Pro (6/15 people including host). History recording/editing needs viewer paid/trial access plus extension recording consent and separate YouTube switch; Free retains saved history, Resume and deletion.

**Cloudflare Requirements From Current Docs:**

- Use `state.acceptWebSocket(server)` or `ctx.acceptWebSocket(server)`, not `server.accept()`.
- Implement Durable Object methods `webSocketMessage`, `webSocketClose`, and `webSocketError`.
- Expect the constructor to run again after hibernation.
- Expect in-memory state to be reset after hibernation.
- Use `serializeAttachment()` and `deserializeAttachment()` for small per-socket connection state.

No hard IP bans or heavy fingerprinting; unchecked items are proposed, not delivered/current entitlements.
nodes.evidence_excerpt: - **PD4 — free-account farming resistance (owner decision 2026-06-12):** layered and observability-first, no hard IP bans. (1) OAuth-only signup via Google/Discord stays — already the strongest single barrier to mass account creation. (2) App-level rate limits on signup, extension auth exchange, and room create, keyed by IP and /24 subnet. (3) Signup/recent IPs stored only as HMAC hashes (dedicated secret, ~30-day retention) — never raw IPs. (4) A *soft* combined per-IP daily cap on free host-minutes (3x a single user's quota): one household or campus NAT is never falsely blocked, but a farm of free accounts behind one IP stops scaling. (5) Cloudflare Turnstile challenge only when a rate limit trips, not on every signup. Heavier device fingerprinting is deliberately deferred until telemetry shows real abuse.
nodes.rationale: Shared-NAT families/campuses must not be falsely blocked while account farming is measured and bounded.

nodes.label: Stripe cancel and success retain existing lifecycle
nodes.description: Canceling Stripe returns to pricing with the billing period and does not reopen Checkout automatically. Completion uses the existing success page and server/webhook subscription lifecycle.

nodes.label: Website-only continuation with stable server contracts
nodes.description: Only website navigation and presentation change. API payloads, session/cookie contracts, OAuth correlation/PKCE, entitlements, prices, session creation, webhooks, schema, Worker and extension remain. No environment, OAuth-client, secret or Stripe configuration change is required.
nodes.rationale: Continuation reuses established payment and authentication authority instead of introducing new lifecycle or infrastructure state.

nodes.label: Local regression and contextual login evidence
nodes.description: New regression cases failed before fixes. Focused pricing/continuation/OAuth suite passed 52; full website suite passed 963 with 6 existing skips, TypeScript and scoped ESLint passed. Local Plus yearly and Pro monthly login retained exact Google/Discord links. Component HTTP fixtures cover StrictMode, owner/session/price/offer changes, 409, retries, double clicks, background responses and partial-session recovery. Independent review edge cases were reproduced, fixed and re-reviewed.

nodes.label: Real OAuth and Sandbox owner acceptance remains pending
nodes.description: Local OAuth credentials are unavailable; real Google/Discord to Stripe Sandbox to success is unverified. After explicit staging delivery authorization, owner tests guest plan/interval, canceled sign-in and retry, trial terms, used-trial and existing-subscriber cases, and Stripe cancellation. Current staging/main are unchanged by these local checks.
nodes.rationale: Automated component responses and local login rendering do not prove authenticated provider or Stripe behavior.

nodes.label: Checkout continuation code-only rollback
nodes.description: Revert this change to return guests to prior pricing after login. SQL, secrets and Stripe configuration need no rollback; existing Checkout sessions and subscriptions keep the server lifecycle.

nodes.label: October 1 welcome history preparation and October 2 staged acknowledgement
nodes.description: codex/extension-welcome-history starts from staging 73df5668. The October 1 checkpoint initially used a compact once-per-installation introduction explaining Plus/Pro hosting, free joining and saved account history; Settings opened the settings panel, Got it dismissed it, and offscreen restored scroll did not mark it seen. The October 2 follow-up to staging PR #396 supersedes automatic seen behavior: only clicking Got it records an installation-local acknowledgement. Opening, tab navigation, Settings and scrolling do not acknowledge the notice. Subsequent local Settings polish shares switches, preserves popup content scroll and keeps hidden Inbox arrivals unread; the welcome heading dot is removed. The unpacked staging folder is for owner review; browser/user acceptance remains outstanding. No server, protocol, permissions, billing, staging/main or Store change is part of this task. The local Watch follow-up additionally separates provider pagination with preserved depth and full-history server search; actual loaded-extension owner acceptance is still pending. A further local Crunchyroll composer correction isolates native-control visibility and keyboard lifecycle. The owner confirmed it works; normal/fullscreen coverage was not individually recorded. The subsequent local YouTube composer guard still awaits owner acceptance. The next local composer-dismiss follow-up adds visible Close, empty Enter dismissal, draft discard via Close/Alt+C, focused-button Enter routing and non-fullscreen Escape release handling. Chrome keeps fullscreen Escape ownership; no Keyboard Lock permission is requested. Loaded-provider acceptance after Reload remains pending. The original local-only scope statements are historical. PR #397 now delivers the remaining acknowledgement and safeguards to staging; the validated staging-196 ZIP includes explicit Got it and previously staged extension changes. The delivery receipt does not claim all provider/manual acceptance completed, and loaded acknowledgement remains the owner's check.

nodes.label: Missing-history preference defaults on with recording fences
nodes.description: Missing account/browser preference defaults enabled; explicit off remains off and unreadable data remains off. Recording still requires signed-in owner, paid/trial access, lease/session checks and separate YouTube opt-in. The dedicated Settings panel uses shared switches and can stop recording without deleting saved history.

nodes.label: Privacy and Store disclosures precede candidate publication
nodes.description: Before publishing the local welcome/history candidate, deploy matching public privacy text and align Chrome Web Store disclosures. Local implementation and unpacked owner review do not constitute public release.

nodes.label: Watch welcome persists until explicit Got it acknowledgement
nodes.description: The October 2 local follow-up shows the Watch welcome on every opening until Got it is clicked. Only that button saves an installation-local acknowledgement. Tab changes, opening Settings and scrolling do not acknowledge it. Existing automatic seen flags are not migrated, so upgraded installations see the notice again. Recording is independent of welcome opening or dismissal; Settings exposes the existing recording switch. This remains local pending delivery/acceptance.
nodes.rationale: Automatic seen state cannot establish that the user clicked Got it; viewing must not silently acknowledge the notice.

nodes.label: Public privacy and Chrome Web Store data-practice alignment
nodes.description: The local privacy page describes default-on recording. Before public release the public privacy policy and Store listing must match actual data practices. Historical compliance record remains historical; no permissions or API contracts change.
nodes.rationale: Public policy and Store disclosures must describe the actual default-on history data practices before public release.

nodes.label: Recording authority survives default-on preference
nodes.description: Signed-in account ownership, current Plus/Pro or trial, lease/session fences and separate YouTube opt-in apply before capture, catalog discovery and progress dispatch. Disabled recording stops new work without deleting saved history; dispatched requests can finish. Website manual editing, reading and Resume remain unchanged.

nodes.label: Local dedicated Settings panel and popup continuity polish
nodes.description: Subsequent local Settings polish uses one dedicated panel and shared switches for recording, YouTube history and invitation notifications. New Inbox arrivals remain unread while Inbox is hidden. Content scroll survives Settings close and popup reopen; the welcome heading dot is removed. This is a local candidate, with browser/user acceptance outstanding and no staging/main or Store delivery.

nodes.label: Local independent YouTube and Crunchyroll history pagination
nodes.description: Watch initially loads 20 titles per provider and loads 20 more through a button inside that provider expanded list. Server search/date filters cover the entire saved history before pagination; provider counts are full filtered totals. Loaded depth persists independently per provider/query, account and generation across popup reopening and partial-cache-failure retries. Recording, quotas and server contracts remain unchanged. Regression checks and local component preview cover pagination and finding an unloaded title; owner Reload and actual-history acceptance remain outstanding.

nodes.label: Local shared authority fence and cancel-safe provider loading
nodes.description: A shared authority failure hides both provider streams and pending rows until validated network recovery. Canceled loads cannot block a later Load more action. Provider/query/account/generation isolation and retained depth apply during recovery; this local follow-up does not alter recording, quotas or server contracts.

nodes.label: Active Player And Detail Page States
nodes.description: May 26 empirical research distinguishes active video/controls/Katamari from detail-only watch pages without video. A watch route with no player is a waiting state; observation/retry binds media later while room admission can proceed independently.

nodes.label: Bounded MAIN World Metadata Bridge
nodes.description: Schema-3 metadata discovery uses a bounded MAIN-world bridge and background coordinator. Identity-pending progress waits for exact GUID resolution. Requests have deadlines/cancellation/response bounds, at most four active requests, 100 raw seasons, 2000 episode rows per response and a bounded aggregate bundle. Meaningful title interaction triggers collection, never startup/heartbeat/Popup polling or crawling.

nodes.label: Catalog Revision And Context Fences
nodes.description: Server revision, owner/history generation, page/visit, context, deletion and invalidation fences reject obsolete collections. Region change immediately suppresses old exact aggregates; a failed same-region locale refresh retains the committed exact bundle and labels.

nodes.label: Current Object Identity Resolution
nodes.description: Resolve the exact recorded watch GUID to one object and matching version, then one raw season with canonical identifier, then one matching episode row with nonempty canonical identifier and consistent season GUID. Keys use crunchyroll:series:<id>, crunchyroll:season:<identifier> and crunchyroll:episode:<identifier>. Missing/duplicate/inconsistent evidence remains pending; titles, numbers, audio and locale never replace identity.

nodes.label: Katamari Player Control
nodes.description: May 26 live research found the usable player through React stateNode.player._katamariPlayer, while public window.bitmovin may be empty. Prefer Katamari seekToStreamTime/play/pause, with captured Bitmovin and native timeline as bounded fallbacks. Seek can work in playing/paused/rebuffering; stopped/mediaLoading are transitional.

nodes.label: Participant Control Capabilities

nodes.label: How Joining Works
nodes.description: Guest opens Web /room/:roomId, signs in, records membership and redirects to source URL with #anidachiRoom. Extension obtains fresh token from /api/rooms/:roomId/connect and connects to Worker; client-provided identity is never authority.

nodes.label: How Login Works
nodes.description: Custom website OAuth uses Supabase tables and own HttpOnly access/refresh cookies. Extension launchWebAuthFlow obtains one-time code and exchanges extension-scoped tokens; background owns refresh/reconciliation. Website access expiry is independent. Probe refresh cookie only for explicit logout/account change without rotation; transient failures preserve cached identity but privileged actions return retryable error until verified token. Startup reconciliation and noninteractive auth fallback handle inactive extension/cookie policy. Secrets never reach extension.

nodes.label: How Playback Sync Works
nodes.description: Host sends state/play/pause/seek; Worker accepts state only from host; viewers receive it and extension compares expected time, ignoring small drift and correcting larger drift. Shared protocol, Worker validation and extension drift logic change together.

nodes.label: How Realtime Rooms Work
nodes.description: Each room maps to one Durable Object holding live participants/host state/chat/reactions/camera/P2P signaling. Durable business data remains in Postgres; per-second playback must not be written there.

nodes.label: How Room Creation Works
nodes.description: Extension sends authenticated metadata to Web POST /api/rooms; Web saves durable Supabase room and returns roomId/token/shareableLink. Extension joins Worker /ws/:roomId?roomToken=... and Worker derives identity/role from verified token. Unauthenticated Worker creation is disabled in commercial mode; investigate Web first on create failure.

nodes.label: How Video And Audio Work
nodes.description: Extension owns WebRTC capture and targeted P2P_SIGNAL offers/answers/ICE/voice/renegotiate/restart/bye through Worker; direct/STUN preferred with Cloudflare TURN fallback. September legacy 2-4 room baseline and September 8 local 4/6/15 participants, four cameras, 4/6/8 microphone target are historical implementation/acceptance context; local experiments do not prove distributed/TURN/device release readiness. LiveKit/SFU requires a new explicit product/infrastructure decision.

nodes.label: Watch page AggregateRating removal

nodes.label: Priority page stability through November 2
nodes.description: Until about 2026-11-02 keep titles, H1s and URLs unchanged on /, /watch-anime-together and /guides/best-anime-to-watch-with-friends.
nodes.rationale: Keep priority pages stable while Google moves them from apex to www.

nodes.label: Ranking indexation and product safety
nodes.description: Do not risk current ranking, indexation or core product flows. Allowed changes enrich existing URLs in place; add non-SEO or owner-approved docs/tools/pages; improve analytics attribution and agent rules; and stop false freshness while keeping discovery sitemaps live.
nodes.rationale: Protect established rankings, discovery and current product behavior.

nodes.label: Ranked URL stability
nodes.description: Public marketing URLs are already ranked. Do not change paths, slugs, redirects or canonical targets to another page; enrich copy, CTA and schema on the same path.
nodes.rationale: Do not force Google to reassociate ranked URL equity.

nodes.label: Owner approval and GSC evidence gate
nodes.description: Without explicit owner approval plus GSC evidence, forbid 301/merge/retire; slug/path renames or canonical retargets; new noindex on marketing URLs; deletion of cohort/force-index sitemap during Coverage recovery; shrinking footer/nav crawl paths; high-traffic H1/intent rewrites; and checkout/auth/room/billing behavior changes beyond optional metadata.
nodes.rationale: High-impact URL, indexation and product changes require explicit owner approval and evidence.

nodes.label: Feature requests public feedback form
nodes.description: /feature-requests is an owner-approved additive public product feedback form, not SEO growth bait.

nodes.label: Keep and Enrich winner queue
nodes.description: While frozen, run seo:portfolio and default to Keep/Enrich. Enrich winners on the same URL with CTR metadata, answer-first copy, mid CTA and product truth. Treat Merge/301 suggestions as report-only; strengthen internal links toward the owner page instead of redirecting. Keep FORCE_INDEX_URL_PATHS and /force-index-sitemap.xml advertised until Coverage recovers.
nodes.rationale: Improve existing winners while maintaining stable ranked paths during the freeze.

nodes.label: Force index discovery sitemap
nodes.description: Keep FORCE_INDEX_URL_PATHS from apps/web/lib/force-index-urls.ts and /force-index-sitemap.xml advertised until Coverage recovers.
nodes.rationale: Preserve discovery for the recovering cohort.

nodes.label: SEO freeze exit criteria
nodes.description: All required for lifting: documented 30/60/90-day review of force-index cohort against GSC Coverage; material decrease in Discovered-not-indexed or owner acceptance of residual; publishing gate still applied for every net-new URL without renaming ranked URLs; and an explicit owner freeze-lift note in this document.
nodes.rationale: Freeze exit requires cohort evidence, publishing discipline and explicit owner decision.

nodes.label: Net-new URL publishing gate
nodes.description: Every net-new URL keeps an owned-query check, parent hub plus two inbound links and rejection below 10 monthly searches. Never satisfy publication by renaming ranked URLs.
nodes.rationale: New URLs still require distinct demand and internal discovery after freeze exit.

nodes.label: GSC Coverage cohort review
nodes.description: Review force-index cohort at 30/60/90 days using GSC Coverage distinctions Indexed, Discovered-not-indexed and Crawled-not-indexed. Freeze exit requires material reduction in Discovered-not-indexed unless owner accepts residual.

nodes.label: SEO portfolio audit
nodes.description: Run pnpm --filter @anidachi/web seo:portfolio, optionally with -- --days 28 --out ./tmp/seo-portfolio.json. Report covers complete public route inventory from static discovery and animeList, GSC page and query-by-page cannibalization candidates, GA4 sessions/organic sessions/key events by landing path, and Keep/Enrich/Merge/301/Review suggestions.

nodes.label: Google Marketing OAuth

nodes.label: Selective staging-to-main delta promotion
nodes.description: Correct the batch on staging, then apply only its deltas to a main-based branch; never merge all staging or copy complete staging marketing pages because of mechanical helper changes.

nodes.label: Website release exclusion boundary
nodes.description: Exclude cardless trial, subscription UI, Netflix runtime/history, local onboarding/overlay changes, Worker, extension, protocol, migrations and deployment workflows. Verify the final main diff preserves every excluded plane.

nodes.label: Footer overlap preservation

nodes.label: Netflix long-distance page overlap preservation

nodes.label: Fate guide JSX apostrophe fix

nodes.label: notOnCrunchyroll film product truth

nodes.label: getSeoSiteOrigin

nodes.rationale: An old apex environment value should not make public SEO outputs contradict the existing redirect.

nodes.label: getResolvedSiteOrigin
nodes.description: Preserve configured deployment origin for runtime consumers, including Gmail OAuth callback fallbacks.

nodes.label: Runtime origin preservation boundary
nodes.description: This patch changes no OAuth allowlist, cookie, Stripe return URL, extension endpoint or environment variable. Do not use NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL changes as a shortcut without checking runtime consumers and explicit Gmail callback configuration.

nodes.label: Vercel apex redirect observation
nodes.description: Read-only inspection recorded www.anidachi.app destination, null redirectStatusCode and live HTTP 307. The domain-level rule precedes the repository permanent redirect.

nodes.label: Authorized same-target Vercel 308 change
nodes.description: After separate production authorization, change only the existing apex-to-www domain redirect status to 308, retaining destination, path and query. Do not reverse direction, change DNS or submit Search Console Change of Address.
nodes.rationale: Provide a permanent signal for the existing redirect direction without moving to a different host.

nodes.label: Guide consolidation permanent 308 status
nodes.description: The four guide consolidations use Next.js permanent: true, which produces 308 rather than the 301 wording in the SEO plan.

nodes.label: Website release verification gates
nodes.description: Run web typecheck, tests, lint, production-mode build and pnpm dev:check; inspect rendered metadata/JSON-LD, both sitemaps, redirects, unsupported film pages and all ten tools.

nodes.label: Gated noindex staging
nodes.description: Keep staging password-gated, noindex and excluded from its sitemap throughout verification and release.

nodes.label: Owner authorization for production promotion
nodes.description: Review the exact main candidate and record tests, staging/preview evidence, exclusion diff, docs and Graphify status in its PR; do not merge before owner authorization.

nodes.label: Post-authorization production verification
nodes.description: Deploy the accepted main candidate, apply authorized same-target Vercel 308, verify a single apex-to-www redirect preserving paths/queries, www HTTP 200, matching www canonical/OG/schema/sitemaps and noindex staging. No extension Store release or Stripe change is needed.

nodes.label: Selective website rollback
nodes.description: Revert the selective promotion or redeploy preceding accepted main revision without database/billing rollback. Restore prior domain status if needed while retaining www destination; permanent redirects may be cached.

nodes.label: Runtime origin preservation
nodes.description: Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL and getResolvedSiteOrigin() unchanged for runtime consumers, including Gmail OAuth callback fallbacks; changing the shared environment value is not an SEO fix.
nodes.rationale: SEO canonical normalization must preserve runtime and OAuth callback behavior.

nodes.label: Vercel apex redirect authorization
nodes.description: After separate production authorization, change only the existing Vercel apex-to-www redirect status from 307 to 308; preserve destination, paths and queries. This is a scoped approval-dependent operation, not evidence of deployment.
nodes.rationale: Make the existing host redirect permanent while preserving its routing behavior.

nodes.label: Selective website release contract reference
nodes.description: Selective release contract referenced at docs/releases/seo/2026-10-12-selective-website-release.md.

nodes.label: Portfolio audit limits
nodes.description: Audit does not replace GSC Coverage Indexed/Discovered-not-indexed/Crawled-not-indexed, manual claim verification before Merge/301, owner approval before URL removal/redirect, or URL stability. Merge/301 must not ship without owner approval and evidence; prefer never moving ranked paths.
nodes.rationale: Audit action suggestions do not authorize redirects or replace indexing evidence.
